title: Bombay Sapphire steps up E1 partnership with Miami GP naming rights
article_text:
Bombay Sapphire has expanded its partnership with the UIM E1 World Championship, becoming the title partner of the Miami Grand Prix 2026 as the all-electric powerboat racing series prepares for its season finale in Biscayne Bay on November 13–14.

The event, officially named the Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami GP 2026, represents a further step in the brand’s growing association with E1. Bombay Sapphire already serves as the championship’s official gin partner and the presenting partner of the E1 Blue Impact Championship.

Under the agreement, the brand will receive prominent integration across the event’s identity, including its official title, logo and promotional campaigns. The partnership will also extend to consumer engagement initiatives across Miami, taking the brand beyond conventional event sponsorship.

A key feature of the collaboration will be BOMBAY SAPPHIRE Club Blue, a premium hospitality experience hosted aboard a private Team Brady yacht at E1 Ocean Club. The activation will feature actress Meghann Fahy as co-host, alongside a DJ performance by Brittany Sky.

Commenting on the expanded partnership, Jamie Copas, Chief Executive Officer, E1 said, “We’re delighted that our long-term partnership with Bombay Sapphire continues to grow and for them to now become title partner for the Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami GP 2026 race double-header. We look forward to working with Bombay Sapphire to bring the partnership to life in Miami as we gear up for a landmark event, with the Championship’s first-ever double-header set to bring the 2026 season to a thrilling close.”

Tara King, Senior Director, North America, Bombay Sapphire, added, “Bombay Sapphire’s ‘Step Into The Blue’ is our invitation to immerse in the beauty of life, and E1 is the ultimate expression of that. This is a fresh addition to the global sports category, bringing all-electric raceboat competition to waterfront cities around the world and drawing attention to the waters that make the sport possible. We brought ‘Step Into The Blue’ to life on the waterfront during E1’s North American debut last year, and we’re excited to build on what we started together. As Title Partner in Miami, we’re bringing that same spirit of discovery beyond the water and into the city – with the Bombay Sapphire Sparkling Lemon as the championship’s official cocktail, we’re giving new audiences an approachable way to discover gin and join the race weekend celebrations across Miami.”

The partnership also builds on Bombay Sapphire’s involvement in the E1 Blue Impact Championship, which recognises teams contributing to aquatic ecosystem conservation and restoration. The Miami double-header will bring the 2026 E1 season to a close, combining electric powerboat racing with entertainment and premium hospitality.

title: An Se-young Claims 11th Title, Sets Historic Record
article_text:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Kim Ga-eul] Even China applauded the performance of 'world's strongest' An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance).

Chinese media outlet 'Sohu.com' reported on the 10th, 'An Se-young set a new record by winning her 11th title of the season. China added 1 gold and 1 silver medal at this tournament.'

The 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) concluded. The biggest focus was undoubtedly whether An Se-young would claim victory. An Se-young has dominated the season with overwhelming skill. World No. 1 An Se-young, who entered the tournament with high expectations, secured the top spot without surprises. She defeated Yamaguchi Akane (world No. 2, Japan) in the final with a game score of 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16), claiming her 11th international singles title of the season. An Se-young matched Kento Momota (Japan)'s 2019 record of 11 single-season titles and became the first player in history to achieve the feat in consecutive seasons.

Sohu.com stated, 'The women's singles final, highly anticipated between An Se-young and Yamaguchi, saw An Se-young take the first game 21-12 with long rallies and precise shots. Yamaguchi won the second set 21-15 with persistent movement and rhythm changes. In the decisive game, An Se-young defended critical points to win 21-16 after a fierce battle. She closed the match with a final score of 2-1. With this victory, An Se-young became the first player in badminton history to win 11 or more titles in two consecutive seasons, continuing to write her own legend.'

Other champions at the tournament included Victor Lai (Canada) in men's singles, Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae in men's doubles, Hirokami Rui and Hovara Sayaka (Japan) in women's doubles, and Zhang Fanfang and Wei Yaxin (China) in mixed doubles.

Sohu.com added, 'China swept gold and silver medals in mixed doubles. Host nation South Korea won both women's singles and men's doubles. Canada and Japan each secured gold and silver medals. Leveraging home advantage, South Korea emerged as the biggest winner of the tournament.'

Reporter Kim Ga-eul epi17@sportschosun.com

title: XEFI saves Team TotalEnergies, becoming primary title sponsor
article_text:
The ailing Team TotalEnergies UCI ProTour road cycling team has been saved from oblivion and will go forward as XEFI, after the eponymous French IT firm struck a new sponsorship contract that will keep the organization afloat.

XEFI has agreed to a three-year deal to become the new primary title sponsor of the team Vendée Cyclisme, the company of former cyclist Jean-René Bernaudeau, which is one of the most prominent teams on the second-tier ProTour circuit.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Founded in 2000 by Bernaudeau, TotalEnergies has been the primary title sponsor of the team since 2021, after it acquired the previous title sponsor, Direct Energie.

Now, XEFI takes up the title sponsor position, granting the team stability for what Bernaudeau calls a ‘medium-term project ’.

TotalEnergies has pulled back from its title sponsorship of the team, but not from cycling as a whole, as it remains a commercial partner of the Tour de France, and a prominent jersey sponsor of the Netcompany Ineos WorldTour team.

The newly renamed XEFI team will compete in the secondary ProTour once again in 2027. However, second-tier status has not affected the team’s visibility on the sport’s biggest stage.

As a French team, Vendée Cyclisme has competed in the Tour de France every year since its foundation in 2000, even during its years on the ProTour circuit, as it qualified as a wildcard selected by the race’s organizer, Amaury Sports Organization.

It is that factor that likely forms a core part of XEFI’s investment, with the opportunity for national (and international) branding visibility without the cost of sponsoring an elite WorldTour team, offering a strong value proposition.

Indeed, the success of Jordan Jegat at the Tour de France, for example, was likely a key motivator.

Jegat secured a top-10 finish in the Tour de France general classification, illustrating the commercial platform that the team can still offer, despite its second-tier status.

That was the second consecutive 10th-placed finish for Jegat at the Tour de France for Team TotalEnergies, and also followed a stage win in 2024 for Anthony Turgis.

Title sponsorship such as this is vital for cycling teams at all levels of the sport, the majority of which are almost entirely sponsor-funded.

Cycling’s heavy reliance on sponsorship revenue, and that spending’s direct correlation with rider contract spending, has created a catch-22 situation where winning races requires top riders, access to top riders requires significant sponsorship revenue, and sponsorship revenue can only be grown by winning races.

This has effectively stratified the WorldTour peloton, with the top six-to-eight teams, backed by high-profile sponsors, billionaire investment, or sovereign wealth financing, performing at a level that the other sides, which rely on less lucrative sponsorship deals and, in many cases, face an annual struggle just to continue operations, cannot.

Vendée Cyclisme, naturally, is part of the latter category, and its flirtation with bankruptcy this year, staved off by XEFI, is a clear illustration of the impact sponsors pulling funding can have.

This dynamic was dissected earlier this year on the Sportcal Podcast, wherein GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and head of data Gordon Berry discussed the varying perspectives on cycling sponsorship, where money in cycling comes from, and how teams can improve sponsorship values by maximizing their resources.

title: British Esports secures American Express Global Business Travel
article_text:
The British Esports Federation has signed a multi-year partnership with American Express Global Business Travel, naming the business travel company as its travel and events sponsor.

The agreement makes Amex GBT British Esports’ strategic commercial partner for travel management, travel agency and event agency services in competitive gaming. The two organisations will create travel offers and packages for players, teams and the businesses around them. They will also explore academy programmes, new event concepts and intellectual property, and develop travel products specific to esports.

The deal runs for an initial three years, with the option to extend from 1st June 2029.

It follows the opening of the British Arena in Sunderland, a 15,000 sq ft multi-use venue. It has a main stage theatre with capacity for 200 seated or 400 standing, a 17m LED screen, broadcast studios, 5G connectivity and 550 sq m of outdoor activation space. British Esports is also expanding its team ahead of a busy 2027 calendar that includes the Esports Nations Cup, the International Defence Esports Games and DreamHack Birmingham.

Travel is becoming a bigger part of the sector’s operations. Great Britain teams compete in international tournaments, and visiting teams train and compete at British Esports’ facilities in Sunderland, including the National Esports Performance Campus. Major UK esports events are also held at venues such as The O2 in London and the NEC in Birmingham. The League of Legends World Championship Final at The O2 in 2024 contributed more than £12m to the economy.

Founded in 2016, British Esports is the national body for esports in the UK and a founding member of the International Olympic Committee’s Esports and Gaming Liaison Group.

Chester King, President of British Esports, said, “We’re excited to be partnering with a leading name in business travel to strengthen our approach to travel and events together. This partnership is particularly exciting because it gives us the chance to build better travel and event experiences for our players and partners.“

“By offering workshops, events, academy programmes and an array of travel solutions with Amex GBT, we can help elevate these areas and offer greater opportunities to the industry. With our British Arena ready to open and more major events going from strength to strength, we look forward to expanding in this area in the future.”

Gerardo Tejado Donde, Senior VP, Professional Services at Amex GBT, said, “Esports is an exciting, vibrant sporting sector that brings together teams, players and brands at fantastic events for their growing community. Partnering with British Esports means we can work alongside the people who know esports best and use those insights to build bespoke travel and event experiences around how this community moves, from tournament weekends to industry gatherings.”

title: ‘I couldn’t move’ – Jannik Sinner lifts lid on ‘strange’ knee injury, weight loss, and ‘worst’ part of his recovery
article_text:
Jannik Sinner has admitted there were days when he “couldn’t move at all” due to the severity of his knee injury.

The Italian has been sidelined with this issue since retaining his Wimbledon title back in mid-July. In early October, after pulling out of the entire North American hardcourt swing and the Asian Swing, Sinner decided to shut down his season in a bid to be fit for the 2027 Australian Open.

The 25-year-old, who has since lost his No 1 ranking to Alexander Zverev, is looking at the bigger picture and trying to build a career that lasts at least another 10 years or so.

On Wednesday, the five-time major winner released a new episode on his YouTube channel titled ‘Jannik Sinner Unfiltered – Health & Recovery’.

In it, he shows himself seeking medical expertise in Lyon, flying back to Monte Carlo for physio work, treatment and training, and meeting up with Darren Cahill, who has just left his team after several successful years together.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Sinner also lifts the lid on just how hard it has been for him to be away from the ATP Tour, not being physically fit, and how it is affecting his life off the court.

He says in the video, “We flew today to Lyon; tomorrow we have some checks for the knee, and we’ll see what the doctor says and hopefully get some good news. Good news would mean that in some weeks we can charge it fully and we can prepare properly for Australia.

“That would be awesome, but I had days where I felt nothing, and I could play without any problems, and then I had days where I couldn’t move at all. So very strange, but tomorrow we have a check. I have my doctor here as well, and also part of the team, and then we see how it goes tomorrow.”

In the clip, a doctor is heard saying Sinner has “lost a lot of weight, a lot of muscles”, while the former world No 1 spoke about how tough it is that his season was taken away from him.

Moreover, Sinner revealed that he had his tonsils removed some “weeks ago” and he “lost a lot of weight”, which is why his face looks “quite dry”.

Incidentally, after winning five Masters 1000 events in a row this year, he looked primed to have a strong final few months of the season after winning Wimbledon. But it wasn’t to be.

He added, “The worst part for me about this injury is that I cannot compete; I cannot play tennis. Also, my life outside of tennis is a bit more limited because of the simple fact that I cannot do things that I really like because I want to protect my knee in the best possible way I can.

“I’m not gonna lie, it’s also tough to see other players play, and I cannot compete also because the season I’ve had has been an incredible season until the moment when everything happened, and it switches from a very, very positive season to a very tough ending and season, even though I had a lot of success.”

title: Coco Gauff criticises ‘stupid’ WTA Finals rules and hints they could change after Linda Noskova loss
article_text:
Coco Gauff criticised the WTA Finals format and dropped a hint that it could change in 2027 after her loss to Linda Noskova in Indian Wells.

The two-time Grand Slam champion was beaten 6-3, 6-3 by world No 8 Noskova in her second round robin match at the 2026 WTA Finals on Tuesday.

Noskova’s victory over Gauff secured her qualification for the semi-finals after she downed Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4 in her opening match.

Gauff defeated Jessica Pegula 6-4, 6-7(5), 6-2 in her first match, and she could miss out on progressing from the group even if she wins her final round robin match against Kostyuk.

Pegula beat Kostyuk 6-2, 7-5 on Tuesday, and if the 32-year-old American overcomes Noskova in her third match, she will join the Czech in the last four — and Gauff will be eliminated regardless of her result against Kostyuk.

World No 10 Kostyuk cannot advance to the semi-final stage after her two straight-set losses. The 24-year-old Ukrainian was the first alternate at the WTA Finals, and she replaced world No 1 and reigning champion Elena Rybakina — who withdrew due to illness.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Gauff holds a 4-2 head-to-head record against Kostyuk, while Noskova has a 3-1 edge from her previous meetings with Pegula.

In a post-match interview with reporters, Gauff was asked if she will think about the qualification scenarios ahead of her third match.

“I’m just gonna focus on the next match,” the 22-year-old American replied. “The scenarios — I mean, I know they make sense, but they’re kinda stupid (laughs).

“I mean, I know it’s like the point thing, and the sets and all of that, but it’s like, I’m just trying to win a match.

“If I win my match and I still don’t qualify, I’m like, ‘It’s okay, it’s cool.’

“Yeah, actually, next year… I’m looking forward to next year. I can’t say much, but everybody knows it has to change.”

World No 4 Gauff is aiming to win her second WTA Finals title, having triumphed at the prestigious season-ending event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in 2024. She is making her fifth consecutive WTA Finals appearance.

title: Pools Announced for Dubai 7s
article_text:
The 2026-27 HSBC SVNS Series hosts the first of six legs on Nov. 28-29 in Dubai, UAE. The pools have been announced and the schedule is forthcoming. The USA Women’s 7s Team will compete in Pool B alongside Australia, France and Spain. [lead photo: Alex Ho @hoiho_photo]

There are eight core teams for both the men’s and women’s competition that will feature in all six legs. Thus, each tournament will split into two pools of four teams. For the series opener, the USA Women will compete in Pool A against Australia, France and Spain. The Eagles are coming off a pre-season tour to New Zealand, where the extended squad faced Japan, France, Australia, Fiji and a New Zealand developmental side. Among some young faces looking for their first selection to an HSBC SVNS Series team was Ilona Maher, who has rejoined the residents in pursuit of an LA28 Olympics roster spot.

The USA Men have played their way onto the championship circuit as well and will compete in Pool A alongside South Africa, Australia and Argentina in Dubai.

The tournament format has teams play their pool games on day one, and then the top-two teams out of both pools advance to the Cup semifinals on day two. The bottom-two teams in each pool move into the Plate bracket. Stay tuned for a detailed schedule and streaming options. Once Dubai crowns its champions, the field relocates to Cape Town, South Africa, on Dec. 5-6 for round two. See the full series schedule here.

Teams accrue standings points throughout the six-tournament series, which culminates with New York 7s held in Harrison, N.J., on March 13-14. There is special impetus for U.S. fans to show up to Sports Illustrated Stadium, as the occasion is a precious opportunity to see both American 7s teams compete in front of a home crowd. Buy tickets.

Following the conclusion of New York 7s, the International fields will then be seeded into a World Championship series, which includes April/May stops in Hong Kong; Valladolid, Spain; and Bordeaux, France.

title: New Study Reports Rising Fortune 500 Investment in Women’s Sports
article_text:
Big business is buying in. This week’s third annual Gather study found Fortune 500 sponsorship on the rise across the WNBA, NWSL, and PWHL.

The share of Fortune 500 companies backing women’s sports hit 16%, up from 13% over 2025. The number additionally grew at 3.8 times the rate of the men’s side.

Across 205 deals, the number of women’s sports sponsors grew 18% while total sponsorships jumped 38%. Significantly, corporations like CVS Health, Sprouts, and State Street dealing exclusively with women’s teams.

Despite the upticks, the gender divide remains wide — though analysts predict women’s sports will continue to see gains across industries.

Fortune 500 brands back men’s sports at 36%, with the NBA doubling the WNBA’s deals while the NHL outpaced the PWHL by more than nine times.

“We’re going to start to see folks who didn’t have sports deals at all coming to the women’s side, both because it’s a lower dollar entry and because it is fashionable,” Gather’s Head of Innovation David Gaspar told SBJ.

title: Leaked England team to play Japan: Henry Pollock among three surprise starters
article_text:
Steve Borthwick is set to shake up his England team against Japan, with Henry Pollock, Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph all reportedly handed starting roles.

According to The Times, the trio are expected to start Saturday's Nations Championship clash at Allianz Stadium.

England head into the contest following their impressive 45-22 victory over Australia.

However, injuries have forced Borthwick into several changes ahead of next week's showdown with New Zealand.

Pollock is reportedly set to start at number eight after scoring twice against Australia.

The Northampton Saints youngster finished that match on the wing but is expected to return to the back row for his second Test start.

Gloucester's Will Joseph is also set for his first England start, more than four years after making his international debut.

The 24-year-old has reportedly moved ahead of Joe Marchant in the selection race.

Henry Pollock is reportedly set to start at number eight for England against Japan.

Bath centre Max Ojomoh is expected to replace the injured Seb Atkinson at inside centre.

The 25-year-old impressed during England A's 59-24 victory over Argentina XV last Friday.

Borthwick had been weighing up Ojomoh and Fraser Dingwall, but the Bath man has reportedly won that battle.

He could now partner Henry Slade in midfield.

Bodø/Glimt announces collaboration with Amazon Web Services to support its investment in technology
article_text:
Bodø, 10th November 2026 – Bodø/Glimt has entered into a strategic collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS), which will provide the cloud infrastructure to support the club’s investment in data and artificial intelligence (AI).

The collaboration will support the development of data-driven and AI-based solutions across the club’s sporting and commercial operations.

“We found AWS to be forward-thinking, both technologically and culturally. They have strong references and a technology platform that can grow with the club. Just as importantly, their ambition and way of working stood out. We want strategic partners who challenge us, actively contribute to our development and move quickly, as well as provide infrastructure.”

“We are a small organisation, and we intend to remain one. Our ambition is to learn faster, make better decisions and use our resources more effectively than our

competitors. Technology gives us new opportunities to achieve exactly that. Building on AWS will be an important part of our technological development,” Thomassen added.

“With AWS, Bodø/Glimt gains access to the same scalable infrastructure and AI technology used by leading sports clubs and organisations around the world. This can provide a stronger basis for decision-making across the organisation.”

The initiative builds on the club’s wider investment in technology. Earlier this year, Bodø/Glimt established Edge Case Ventures AS, a wholly owned company focused on developing and implementing technology within and around the club. The club has also announced a strategic collaboration with BearingPoint covering data, AI and digital development, alongside the appointment of a new leader responsible for data and AI.

“We are building step by step. The most important thing is to maintain control of our strategic direction and ownership of our own data, while working with some of the strongest technology environments. We believe that combining a small internal team with strong strategic partners can give a club like Bodø/Glimt a significant competitive advantage.”

title: Japan want 'the sky to fall in' at Twickenham
article_text:
Head coach Eddie Jones says Japan are drawing inspiration from Italy, who beat England for the first time in March, as the Brave Blossoms attempt to heap pressure back on Steve Borthwick with their own landmark win on Saturday.

Jones was sacked by England in December 2022 after a miserable autumn which ended in a 27-13 Twickenham defeat by South Africa and jeers from the home fans.

The Australian, 66, hopes to cause similar unrest on his return to Allianz Stadium this weekend.

"We're massive underdogs," Jones told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"We've got to find a way to disrupt an England side that's looking at New Zealand next week [England play the All Blacks on 21 November] and sometimes may be a little bit distracted.

"Our opportunity is to get in there, cause some havoc, cause some chaos, put off their game, get the crowd booing. Then the sky starts to come in on Twickenham and you never know what can happen.

"We've seen it happen with Italy and other countries."

Japan have lost all six of their previous Test meetings with England, most recently going down 54-19 on their autumn visit two years ago.

However Italy, who won for the first time in 33 attempts earlier this year, and Fiji, who broke their duck with a 30-22 success in 2023, have both secured maiden victories over England during Borthwick's reign.

Jones believes England's players are uniquely susceptible to pressure, given a level of scrutiny which is unprecedented in the rest of the global game.

A run of five successive defeats earlier this year, combined with reports of a rift between players and coaches, raised the stakes for England before Sunday's meeting with Australia.

However, Borthwick's players, who had insisted that the squad remains united, delivered an impressive 45-22 victory to vindicate their coach.

"The noise does get to the team and it can be pretty loud in England," said Jones, for whom Borthwick worked as an assistant during a previous stint with Japan and then with England.

"You've got a lot of newspapers, a lot of media, probably more than any other country in the world. Sometimes that can weigh down on the players and it's the job of the leadership to get the players thinking straight.

"Steve's an outstanding coach and a very intelligent man, and a really good coach. So I've got the highest respect for him."

England back row Henry Pollock scored two tries after replacing the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time against Australia, and has been tipped to make only his second start for his country on Saturday.

Having also scored a hat-trick off the bench against Fiji in July, Pollock is averaging a try every 22 minutes in the Nations Championship.

However, Jones believes the 21-year-old's sky-high strike-rate is not the best measure of him as a player.

"I wouldn't look too much into it," he said of Pollock's two scores against Australia.

"Everyone was licking the ice cream on Sunday. They were on the front foot, everyone's lining up to run the ball, there's no pressure in the game.

"He's a fast back rower, he got the ball in space and he's a talented player, there's no doubt about it, but you couldn't read into it any more than that."

Fly-half Ryunosuke Ito was plucked from university rugby by Jones, and made his debut against Italy in July without having ever played a professional match.

Ito scored his own solo try against Australia in August, neatly stepping through the Wallabies defence., external

However the 21-year-old fourth-year student, who has established himself as Jones' first-choice fly-half, is required by Meiji University for a collegiate competition, meaning he is missing the northern hemisphere leg of Japan's Nations Championship campaign.

Ito will join top-flight Tokyo side Suntory Sungoliath next season, who have former New Zealand captain Sam Cane and Ireland and British and Irish Lions wing James Lowe in their squad.

"That's the uniqueness of Japanese rugby," added Jones.

title: Steve Borthwick approaches milestone as England head coach
article_text:
Some people will question how has he survived this long, but the fact of the matter is that Steve Borthwick will become only fourth England head coach to get to 50 Tests in charge when his team play Japan in the fifth round of the Nations Championship at Allianz Park on Saturday.

Recently, in response to accusations in a newspaper article that he had created a toxic environment, Borthwick revealed that some former England head coaches had sent him a private message of support.

Only Sir Clive Woodward (84), Eddie Jones (81) and Stuart Lancaster (52) have led England in more Tests, and you’d assume it was at least one of those three, or Geoff Cooke, whose record of 49 Tests he’ll overtake on Saturday, who told him, ‘been there, got the t-shirt’.

Borthwick was appointed as Eddie Jones’ successor on 19 December, 2022, nine months out from Rugby World Cup 2023, having worked as Jones’ number two previously, with England and Japan.

At the time, England were ranked fifth in the world, as they are now, but their present rankings score of 86.99 is 3.33 points higher. Something to cling to, perhaps, when people question whether England have made any progress under him.

Borthwick’s reign began with a 29-23 home defeat to Scotland at the start of the 2023 Six Nations, with Max Malins scoring the first points and tries under the ex-England lock and captain.

Ten of the 23 players who featured that day – Ellis Genge, Jamie George, captain Maro Itoje, Ollie Chessum, Ben Curry and Ben Earl in the forwards and Jack van Poortvliet, Marcus Smith, Freddie Steward and Joe Marchant in the backs – are in Borthwick’s current squad preparing for the visit of Japan.

Borthwick only had to wait for his second match to chalk up the first of his 29 wins in charge, a 31-14 victory at home to Italy, before England followed it up with a 20-10 win on the road in Cardiff.

England were quickly brought back down to earth after suffering a record 53-10 humiliation at home to France, which was followed by a 29-16 defeat to Ireland in Dublin and a fourth-place finish in the Championship.

To the surprise of many, England finished third at the 2023 World Cup, only losing to the eventual champions South Africa by a point in the semi-finals.

Borthwick’s stock had undoubtedly risen but the style of play under him meant he would be given little leeway if results went wrong.

England moved up a place to third in the 2024 Six Nations but a 3-0 series defeat to New Zealand that summer showed how much ground England had to make up on the top teams before they could be considered one themselves.

By the end of the year, there was more disquiet as England blew a chance to beat Australia, losing a Twickenham thriller 42-37, and were then a distinct second-best to the Springboks.

England kicked off the 2025 Six Nations with a defeat to Ireland but a run of four straight wins, two of them by a point, left them just one point behind champions France in the final standings.

Wins over Argentina, twice, and USA kept the chariot rolling forward into November, where a clean sweep was achieved against Australia, Fiji, the All Blacks and Argentina.

When Wales were brushed aside, 48-7, on a memorable debut for Henry Pollock, England had reeled off 12 wins on the bounce – the third longest winning streak in the men’s team history.

The euphoria of that run, though, was quickly extinguished when a 30-21 Calcutta Cup defeat to Scotland was followed by a record 42-21 home loss to Ireland and then came the nadir of Borthwick’s time in charge, a first-ever defeat to Italy.

England salvaged some pride in going down 48-46 to France in their best display of attacking rugby under Borthwick but there was no escaping the fact that England had suffered their worst Six Nations in history.

The message from the RFU after an internal review was to keep clam and carry on, with Borthwick being awarded a contract through to the end of the 2028 Six Nations.

And since then, England have won three of their first four games in the inaugural Nations Championship.

Borthwick has a 59.2% win success rate from his 49 tests as head coach, the lowest of those with as many or more appearances, with England scoring 1,445 points and 183 tries and conceding 1,078 points and 133 tries during his tenure.

Woodward, Jones and Cooke all have 70%+ winning percentages, while Lancaster, even with a disastrous home World Cup in 2015, won 63.5% of his 52 Tests.

title: England must collaborate with clubs for Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry's recovery, says Kevin Sinfield
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry will be carefully managed between now and the World Cup as England look to give two key personnel the best possible chance of being available for the tournament.

Feyi-Waboso will miss the rest of the autumn because of an ankle injury sustained in Sunday’s 44-22 mauling of Australia, robbing England of their most dangerous attacking threat.

And British and Irish Lions flanker Curry will sit out all four Nations Championship matches at Allianz Stadium this month after aggravating a long-standing hip condition in training last week.

Both players will travel to next year’s World Cup in Australia if fit but have concerning injury records that paint an uncertain picture over their involvement.

Under the current agreement between England and the Prem clubs, head coach Steve Borthwick now has greater control over the 25 members of his elite player squad, including final say on workload and medical matters.

“The best high-performance environments have the right amount of care and the right amount of challenge,” assistant coach Sir Kevin Sinfield said.

“How Tom’s managed, looked after and supported over this next period of time will be really important for him.

“He’s still a young man and we’re a better squad when he’s around. He’s a world-class player.

“The agreement that’s in place hopefully will ensure brilliant collaboration between club and country so that Tom plays for a long, long time, and he can be at his very best when he’s in and out of camp.

“Manny’s had a run of injuries now and hopefully that can be the last one for some time. I think it’s because of the nature of how he’s put together – he’s that powerful.

“What you tend to find is players either get a load of injuries at the start of their careers or get them towards the back end.

“Hopefully we can get him fully fit for a long period of time and Exeter get to see the best of him too. Again the collaboration is going to be really important for us.”

Feyi-Waboso’s unique ability to beat defenders was on full display at Twickenham and Sinfield described his performance as “world class”, adding “he’s our Jason Robinson” in reference to the cross-code great.

His absence creates a vacancy on the wing for Saturday’s Test against Japan and whoever is selected will be instructed to play to their own strengths.

“There aren’t many Mannys kicking around so to go like for like is difficult,” Sinfield said.

“We can’t ask somebody to come in and play like Manny, but we can ask them to come in and bring the best of themselves.”

Gloucester’s in-form outside back Will Joseph is one of the players looking to fill his boots and Sinfield insists he is ready to take his chance if selected.

“What a player he is,” Sinfield said. “He beats people. He’s got great balance. He’s a good defender with unbelievable power and speed off the mark.

“He’s a special player. Some of the bits he’s done in training have been ‘wow’ moments. He can play.”

title: Grand Slam finalist confirms tennis comeback plans and reveals retirement timeline
article_text:
Ons Jabeur has announced she plans to return to tennis in 2027 and has revealed when she wants to officially hang up her racket.

The three-time Grand Slam finalist said she was taking an indefinite break from tennis in July 2025 as she had not “felt happy on court for some time” and it was time to “take a step back”.

A year ago, Jabeur announced she was expecting her first child, with the 32-year-old then giving birth to her son, Elyan, in April. At the time, the former world No 2 hailed him as a “tiny miracle”.

Fast forward to the present and the Tunisian record-breaker has set her sights on returning to the WTA Tour at some point next year.

While the veteran has not set a specific date or targeted a certain tournament for her comeback, the five-time WTA Tour title winner is not done with the sport yet.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

She told The National, “I’m hoping to come back, hopefully next year. I still don’t know the exact time, but very soon.

“I’m still discovering … my body is a bit changed after the delivery, but I’m definitely coming back and hoping to stay a few more years on tour before actually retiring.

“I’m enjoying every moment, you know; motherhood, it’s been amazing. Definitely will want more sleep, but it’s part of the process. I’m enjoying everything with my son … He actually comes with me when I train. I’m trying to come back slowly.”

Jabeur turns 33 next August, so if she plans on playing for a few more years, the 5ft 6in player could play into her late 30s.

The two-time Wimbledon runner-up, who is the most successful tennis player of all time from Tunisia, will hope to join a distinguished list of stars who won a major after giving birth.

They include Kim Clijsters, Margaret Court, and Evonne Goolagong Cawley, while the likes of Serena Williams, Elina Svitolina, Belinda Bencic and Victoria Azarenka all won WTA Tour titles after becoming a mother.

After the two most successful seasons of her career in 2022 and 2023, Jabeur finished 2024 ranked 42nd in the world and in 2025, that fell to 79.

Whether Jabeur, who reached three major finals between the summer of 2022-23, can enjoy a successful second stage of her career remains to be seen.

title: DP World Tour Q-School: Which Notable Names Earned A Card At Final Stage And Who Missed Out?
article_text:
Former LIV golfer Jose Luis Ballester earned co-medallist honors in the final stage of DP World Tour Q-School 2026, consequently becoming one of 20 players to earn full status at Europe's top table next term.

Ballester tied with fellow Spaniard Rocco Repetto Taylor on 32-under-par following six gruelling rounds at Infinitum's Lakes and Hills Courses, with a final-round 65 from both sealing the deal.

The former Fireballs GC pro wasn't the only LIV man to earn his way onto the DP World Tour in style, though, as Byeong Hun An finished T8th (-28) while reserves John Catlin and Ben Schmidt were among the final cluster of players to pick up a card.

An incredible 25-under was the score required to share 14th place, a number reached by Team Europe's Ryder Cup vice-captain, Edoardo Molinari courtesy of a closing 67.

Other golfers to make an immediate return to the DP World Tour included Australia's Cameron John - who finished solo third on 31-under - plus England's Tom Lewis and Spain's Ivan Cantero (T4th).

While Catlin's eight-under 63 was certainly an impressive feat, Germany's Philipp Katich posted the round of the day to squeeze in on the number.

A remarkable nine-under 62 at the Lakes Course helped him finish alongside Italy's Matteo Cristoni, USA's Jansen Preston and Sweden's Niklas Lemke just above the dotted line.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

But the fact Katich is now on his way to the DP World Tour is wild, especially where he was after four rounds.

As pointed out by Monday Q Info on X, the German was one of seven players to sit T61st (one place outside the cut line) on Monday.

Yet, because of Frank Kennedy's disqualification for damaging a green, Katich was able to play the final two days.

He made the most of that chance with a round of 66 prior to a remarkable showing on Wednesday which secured his promotion.

Meanwhile, Albin Bergstrom, Marcus Helligkilde, Paul Beauvy, Ryan Lumsden, Jannik De Bruyn, Adam Blomme and David Nyfjall completed the group of players to earn full DP World Tour status in 2027.

WHICH PLAYERS EARNED DP WORLD TOUR CARDS VIA Q-SCHOOL?

WHICH BIG NAMES MISSED OUT ON A DP WORLD TOUR CARD AT Q-SCHOOL?

Over 150 players were originally listed in the field for DP World Tour Q-School Final Stage, so naturally plenty of notable names were not going to be successful.

Perhaps the biggest surprise of all was Elvis Smylie, who won the BMW Australian PGA Championship as recently as 2024.

However, the ex-LIV pro ended this week's Q-School test in a tie for 32nd on 22-under, just three strokes off a card, and will now likely try to make his way back via the HotelPlanner Tour or through invites into DP World Tour events next season.

Thomas Pieters also failed to pick up full status on the DP World Tour after ending in a share of 45th on 20-under-par.

The Belgian - who is a six-time DP World Tour winner - will likely rue a one-over round of 73 on Sunday as the primary factor for his disappointment.

Elsewhere, Spain's Pablo Larrazabal and Italy's Renato Paratore finished just outside of the top-50 once all was said and done, two strokes in front of former LIV player Luis Masaveu.

Among the players to miss the cut after round four included Kalle Samooja, Callum Tarren, Dylan Naidoo, Yannik Paul, Frederik Kjettrup, Jinichiro Kozuma, Ross Fisher and Luis Carrera.

title: Will Joseph poised to audition for leading role against Japan in Feyi-Waboso’s absence
article_text:
England need to find a talented understudy for their injured star wing Manny Feyi-Waboso, and are poised to invite Gloucester’s Will Joseph to audition for a leading role against Japan on Saturday. The latter was a travelling reserve for last weekend’s Australia game and appears set for a Test recall four years after being given his debut by the current Brave Blossoms head coach, Eddie Jones.

The 24-year-old Joseph, whose brother Jonathan was a regular in England’s midfield for years, has been in outstanding club form and, as things stand, seems likely to feature in some capacity with injuries forcing Steve Borthwick to reconsider the backline blend that prospered against the Wallabies.

With Feyi-Waboso, Seb Atkinson and George Furbank all sidelined on Saturday, a number of spaces need filling in the matchday 23 and England’s assistant coach Kevin Sinfield believes Joseph, who can operate at both centre and wing, has the talent to seize any opportunity that comes his way. “What a player he is,” said Sinfield, who was knighted earlier this year for his contributions to rugby and Motor Neurone Disease charity fundraising.

“I’ve been really impressed with him in training … having only worked with Will for a little while he’s made a huge mark on everybody. He beats people, he’s got great balance and he’s a good defender with unbelievable power and speed off the mark. He’s a good jackaller, he breaks the line … he’s a special player. Some of the bits he’s done in training have been ‘wow’ moments. He can play.”

Joseph’s only previous cap came in the closing minutes of England’s Test victory against the Wallabies in Brisbane in 2022 when he was a 20-year-old apprentice and Jones was the head coach. The scintillating try he scored for Gloucester at Exeter earlier this season, however, was a striking reminder of his talent and he has also been impressing his teammate Alex Coles on Bagshot’s training pitch. “He rounded someone on the wing in five metres of space and even Henry Pollock, who was on the defensive side against him, celebrated his try because it was that good,” Coles said.

There are plenty of other back-three contenders lurking in England’s squad, including Cadan Murley, Joe Marchant, Noah Caluori and Tobias Elliott, but Joseph’s positional versatility could also boost his cause when it comes to picking a final World Cup squad next year.

That said the uber-talented Feyi-Waboso remains England’s most lethal attacking weapon, with Sinfield describing his performance against Australia, before he came off with an ankle injury at half-time, as “world class”. “He’s our Jason Robinson,” said Sinfield, referencing his fellow cross-code legend.

“He’s frustrated but what a last game it was for him. We can’t ask somebody to come in and play like Manny, but we can ask them to come in and bring the best of themselves. That’s what we’ll be doing this week. We would like whoever comes in to play with a lot of courage, back themselves and, when they’re put in space, to try and take the opportunities that they’re given.”

In the longer term England are already looking at how they can best ensure Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry, whose hip problems have resurfaced, are in prime nick when the 2027 World Cup comes around. It raises the possibility that the Rugby Football Union, under the terms of its agreement with the Prem clubs, may seek to limit the amount of rugby the pair play this season for their respective clubs, Exeter Chiefs and Sale Sharks. “The agreement that’s in place will hopefully ensure brilliant collaboration between club and country,” said Sinfield.

“What you tend to find is players either get a load of injuries at the start of their careers or get them towards the back end. Hopefully we’ve had a good run with Manny now and that can be the last one for some time. We can then get him fully fit for a long period of time and Exeter get to see the best of him, too. Again, the collaboration [with the clubs] is going to be really important for us.”

title: These 20 players just earned a DP World Tour card as LIV Golf stars dominate at Q School
article_text:
It’s one of golf’s most grueling tests and it’s over for another year. For these players, Europe’s top table awaits in 2027…

The DP World Tour Q School results are in.

Teeing up at Infinitum in Spain this week were 156 hopefuls who would play 108 holes over six days in a bid for DP World Tour playing rights next season. This year’s chances were ever so slightly slimmer, with the number of available cards reduced from 20 to 15 plus ties. As it happened, 20 players did exactly that, so who booked their ticket for 2027?

Josele Ballester carded six rounds of 68 or better to finish on 32-under-par to top the leaderboard alongside fellow Spaniard Rocco Repetto-Taylor. Ballester, who joined the professional ranks last year to join Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs team on LIV Golf, made north of $10 million in two years on the league before it was wound down.

Another LIV golfer, Byeong Hun An, who defected to create Korean Golf Club in January, is also in after birdies on four of his last six holes ensured he was comfortably inside the cut-off. “Found a new job,” he posted on X after. John Catlin, who spent a lot of time on LIV as a wildcard, will also be a DP World Tour player next year after a 63 saw him into the top-15.

Elsewhere, Edoardo Molinari might be revolutionizing golf as Luke Donald’s Ryder Cup stats guru these days, but the Italian was a two-time winner in 2010 to earn a spot on Colin Montgomerie’s European team that year at Celtic Manor. Molinari won Q School two years ago, and this year he had to do it the slightly harder way, with a birdie at the 108th and very last hole enough to sneak one of the last cards.

And take a bow, Tom Lewis, because what a rollercoaster this must have been. After missing out at the Second Stage of Q School, the Englishman was on his way home when he received a call to say he could return to take part in a playoff to be an eighth alternate for the final. He only decided to go back because his flight was delayed. As it happens, he won that playoff and enough players withdrew from the final for him to get in. Fast forward a few days later and he’s gone from not even having HotelPlanner Tour status to having a DP World Tour card.

Incredibly, that wasn’t even the most bonkers story from Q School. When Frank Kennedy was booted from the tournament for leaving a “one-foot divot” in the 15th green during the fourth round, his disqualification knocked a couple of players inside the cut line. One of those was German Philipp Katich, who carded a 66 on day five before a round-of-the-day 9-under 62 saw him leap 35 places to get a card on the number.

Right, so who else is in? Let’s take a look. (Before you scroll on – are you looking for a list of big names who didn’t earn a card at Q School? Well, you’ll find that right here.)

The top 15 plus ties after six rounds at Infinitum will earn Category 18 exemption status on the DP World Tour next season. And they are…

You can see the full leaderboard on the DP World Tour website.

title: Charnes elected as permanent PGA of America president
article_text:
Nathan Charnes, the vice president of golf’s PGA of America who has been serving as acting president in recent months, has been elected to the role permanently.

Charnes becomes the organization’s 45th president and succeeds Don Rea Jr., who was stood down from the role in May following a series of missteps during the 2025 Ryder Cup team competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

At the time, the PGA of America’s board of directors announced a leadership transition on the back of Rea's suspension for the last six months of his two-year term.

As part of the change, Charnes was promoted to acting president, while PGA secretary Eric Eshleman, was named interim vice president and has served in a dual role until the election took yesterday.

Eshleman was also elected as the PGA of America’s new permanent vice president, while Jared Barnes was elected secretary.

Charnes will now serve a two-year term representing the organization's more than 30,000 PGA professionals.

He has been involved extensively with the PGA of America for more than 20 years, both locally and nationally.

Rea was elected president of the PGA of America in November 2024 to replace John Lindert, but drew negative headlines in September 2025 for dismissing the abusive and expletive-laden comments thrown at the European team and golfer Rory McIlroy during the Ryder Cup tournament at Bethpage Black.

Responding to a question about the abuse by UK public service broadcaster, the BBC, Rea said: “Well, you’ve got 50,000 people here that are really excited and, heck, you could go to a youth soccer game and get some people who say the wrong thing.

“It happened when we were in Rome [in 2023] on the other side, and Rory understands … things like that are going to happen, and I don't know what was said. But all I know is golf is the engine of good.”

The ensuing public backlash over the remarks saw PGA of America chief executive Derek Sprague apologize to McIlroy and his wife, Erica, who was also subjected to abuse.

A week later, Rea then apologized in an email to PGA of America members, stating “some fan behavior clearly crossed the line” and was “disrespectful, inappropriate, and not representative of who we are as the PGA of America or as PGA of America golf professionals.”

In the email, he admitted that he didn't represent the PGA of America “in the best light with some of my comments.”

Rea also fell under scrutiny for an awkward trophy presentation to the European team for announcing they had retained the Ryder Cup rather than won it, as well as viral clips showing him singing karaoke on the Saturday night of the tournament while the US team was losing.

After the Ryder Cup, Rea was removed from the PGA Tour Policy Board and disappeared from public appearances on behalf of the PGA of America.

Sprague, meanwhile, was announced as the PGA of America’s chief executive in December 2024, becoming the first former president to take up the role.

Sprague served as president from 2014 to 2016 and as honorary president from 2016 to 2018. He also previously served as the PGA vice president and served a two-year term as PGA secretary.

He took over from Seth Waugh, who retired after his contract ended on June 30, 2024.

title: Llewellyn aims to give Wales a hint of Sonny Bill
article_text:
After growing up admiring Sonny Bill Williams in action for New Zealand, Wales centre Max Llewellyn hopes to give the All Blacks some offloading headaches.

Llewellyn is poised to line up at inside centre when Steve Tandy's side welcome New Zealand to Cardiff in the Nations Championship on Saturday (14:10 GMT).

The 6ft 6in Gloucester back grew up watching the double-World Cup winning All Blacks side that featured Dan Carter, Richie McCaw, Ma'a Nonu, Sam Whitelock and Kieran Read.

Yet it was the sizeable frame of dual-code icon Williams - with his ability to free his arms and keep the ball alive - that caught the eye of Llewellyn.

"He was probably someone that I really enjoyed watching when growing up," said the 27-year-old.

"I was a centre, he was a centre and he had a similar frame. I really enjoyed what he did in bringing the offload into rugby.

"That kind of changed the game a bit and was something that I looked at and wanted to emulate."

Llewellyn has done something that not many Welsh rugby players have - he has beaten New Zealand.

That was in the 2019 World Rugby Under-20 Championship in Argentina, but few expect that shock age-grade success to be repeated at senior level this weekend.

Wales have lost 34 successive games in a streak of misery that goes back to 1953, including the agonising one-point loss in 2004 when Llewellyn's father Gareth was in the second row.

Last Saturday's unconvincing 28-21 win against Japan did little to raise hopes of a huge upset, but the centre stresses there is not a defeatist mindset in the Welsh camp.

Llewellyn said: "There's always the belief, especially when you come into work and you are in this Welsh jersey, that you can win.

"We are always willing to deliver everything we can, and above, to make that happen.

"We have been working really hard to make our performances more consistent and better. If we can do that then we will be in a really good spot to be a lot more competitive on Saturday."

Llewellyn was paired with Scarlets' James, 6ft 4in, for the first time against Japan.

It was Steve Tandy's sixth different centre partnership and signalled a move away from Wales' policy of fielding a ball-player in either Joe Hawkins or Ben Thomas in midfield.

"I really enjoyed it. It was the first that I have played with Eddie and I thought we played pretty well together," said Llewellyn.

"The first week of training was about making sure we had the combination locked down and I felt that happened really quickly."

Llewellyn has had 12 on his back just once for Gloucester this season and his only previous start at inside centre for Wales was against England in a World Cup warm-up game in August 2023.

It is where the former Cardiff back sees his long-term future.

He said: "The roles are definitely different. At 12 you get a lot more direct tackles and at 13 you get a few more opportunities when you are out in a bit of space.

"I enjoy playing both and I am fortunate that I can play both, but in the long-term 12 is where I will probably be.

"I think that is where I could get the best out of myself going forward. I enjoy both positions, and they both have different opportunities, but the physical aspect of the game at 12 suits me."

title: Rob Baxter's 'concerning' comment about Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's track record
article_text:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter is keeping his fingers crossed that the surgeon Manny Feyi-Waboso is seeing on Thursday will confirm that he’ll only be out for four to six weeks with the ankle injury he sustained whilst playing for England against Australia on Sunday.

England medics have already publicly declared that that the 23-year-old, who has scored two tries in five appearances this season, will miss the rest of the Nations Championship because of the injury he suffered in the first half of Sunday’s 45-22 win over the Wallabies.

Feyi-Waboso was a victim of a ‘knee-drop’ tackle by Angus Bell and was walking around in a boot post-match, but Baxter says the initial signs are that the injury won’t require an operation.

“He’s in here this morning, getting some treatment,” said Baxter.

“He’s got an appointment tomorrow with the surgeon who’s going to give us a more detailed opinion on all the scan results, etcetera, that he has had. That’ll then decide where it goes.

“I think the balance of opinion at the moment, both from ourselves and England, is that he’s unlikely to require an operation, but I don’t want to confirm that until post tomorrow’s consultations.

“But I think you’re talking, if it’s a decent high ankle sprain, a minimum of four to six weeks really, but it’s just so difficult to know. Manny’s the kind of guy who might be running in a week’s time, and then that changes the whole timescale.

“So, it’s a little early to say too much until there’s a conversation tomorrow because everything could come out really, really positive or you could come out on a negative side.

“The difference between the two is a considerable amount of time. So, I don’t want to say too much and make a statement that was so far wrong it’s ridiculous.”

Feyi-Waboso has scored nine tries in 17 appearances for England, but his progress has been hampered by a string of injuries. He missed the entire 2025 Six Nations with a shoulder injury.

Last year, he picked up a hamstring injury in training before the opening-round win over Wales and was ruled out of the tournament for the second year running.

Baxter adds that, as with England and Lions winger Jack Nowell at the club, they are susceptible to injuries that come in flurries, but there will be long periods when they are injury-free.

“It’s pretty concerning, isn’t it? Jack Nowell was the same when he was here. It’s quite frustrating because you are seeing him over at La Rochelle, and he has had a really high availability.

“But sometimes the way these guys play, they are guys who break tackles and come out the other side of tackles, but they’re always at risk with these kinds of lower limb injuries.

“Because they end up in that situation where they are breaking tackles, and they’re all twisting and exerting pressure and power at awkward times in these types of situations.

“The benefit of having players who are capable of breaking tackles is obviously they’re very dangerous, but the challenge with that, though, is keeping them fit.

“Manny will probably have a few periods where he goes injury-free for considerable lengths of time. It tends to happen like that, you know; injuries tend to come in a bit of a flurry. And then they settle down.”

title: Popov brothers, Blichfeldt and Nalbantova advance in Kumamoto
article_text:
The second day of the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 has brought several positive results for the European contingent, with the final round of 32 matches taking place at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium.

France’s Christo and Toma Junior Popov both secured convincing wins in men’s singles. Top seed Christo defeated Japan’s Minoru Koga 21-14 21-14, while seventh seed Toma Junior beat Chinese Taipei’s Su Li Yang 21-15 21-11.

Denmark’s Mia Blichfeldt also progressed, overcoming China’s Xu Wen Jing in three games. After dropping the second game, Blichfeldt regained control to win 21-14 13-21 21-13.

Another important victory came for Bulgaria’s Kaloyana Nalbantova, who defeated Canada’s Michelle Li 22-20 21-16. The win will be particularly welcome for the 20-year-old, who has endured a difficult few weeks on the World Tour, with several early exits after a successful summer that included reaching the US Open final.

Nalbantova has previously spoken about the mental challenge of dealing with consecutive defeats and finding her rhythm again. Her victory in Kumamoto offers a positive step as she looks to build momentum heading into the remainder of the tournament.

It was not all positive for Europe, however. Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke came close to progressing but eventually fell to India’s Kidambi Srikanth 18-21 21-16 24-22. The Stoeva sisters and Ukraine’s Polina Buhrova were also among the Europeans unable to make it through the opening round.

title: New Japanese Pair Stun Pearly-Thinaah in First-Round Exit at Japan Masters
article_text:
alaysia’s women’s doubles stars Pearly Tan and M. Thinaah suffered a shocking first-round exit at the Japan Masters 2026 after losing to a newly formed Japanese partnership on Tuesday (Nov 10).

The world No. 4 Malaysian pair, who entered the BWF World Tour Super 500 tournament as the second seeds, were defeated by Ririna Hiramoto and Chiharu Shida, ranked 214th in the world, in a three-game battle lasting 64 minutes at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium.

Pearly-Thinaah initially looked set for a promising start after claiming the opening game 21-18. However, the Malaysians struggled to maintain their momentum, allowing the Japanese duo to take control of the match and win the next two games 21-13 and 21-14.

The defeat was particularly surprising as Hiramoto and Shida had only started playing together last month, making this just their third tournament as a partnership. Despite their relatively new combination, Shida brings valuable experience from previously winning several major titles with different partners.

The early exit comes after an impressive year for Pearly-Thinaah, who secured two World Tour titles in 2026, winning the Indonesia Masters in January and the Denmark Open last month.

Despite the setback, the Malaysian duo remain in a strong position to qualify for the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals, scheduled to take place in Hangzhou, China, from Dec 9 to 13. They currently lead the qualification standings, with only the top eight pairs in each category earning a place in the season-ending tournament.

While their Japan Masters title defence has come to an unexpected end, Pearly-Thinaah will now look to regroup and regain their winning momentum ahead of the remaining competitions this season.

title: Indonesian Badminton Players at Kumamoto Masters 2026: Alwi and Ubed Advance, Fajar/Fikri Eliminated
article_text:
KUMAMOTO, Aktualita.co - The struggle of Indonesian badminton players at the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 yielded mixed results. Two men's singles players from the Red and White team, Alwi Farhan and Moh Zaki Ubaidillah, successfully secured spots in the round of 16 after winning their matches on Wednesday (11/11/2026).

Both victories were positive news for Indonesia after two mainstay men's doubles pairs, Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri and Sabar Karyaman Gutama/Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani, were eliminated early.

The BWF World Tour Super 500 tournament, which is taking place at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium, Japan, from November 10–15, 2026, is one of the important opportunities for Indonesian players to collect world ranking points toward the end of the season.

In addition to the men's singles sector, Indonesia also ensured representatives from the women's doubles and mixed doubles categories continued their competition into the second round.

Alwi Farhan appeared solid when facing Chinese Taipei badminton player, Lin Chun-Yi. The young Indonesian player secured a straight-game victory with scores of 21-18 and 21-12.

The match was tight in the first game. Lin was able to match Alwi's play several times before the Indonesian representative took control at crucial points.

Entering the second game, Alwi appeared more dominant. He was able to maintain the rhythm of the game and finished the match in 37 minutes.

The victory sent Alwi to the round of 16 to face Japanese representative, Kenta Nishimoto, on Thursday (12/11/2026).

Meanwhile, Moh Zaki Ubaidillah, or Ubed, had to work much harder to eliminate Brian Yang from Canada.

Ubed lost the first game with a score of 22-24 before turning things around with victories of 28-26 and 21-19 in the next two games.

The match was fierce with several lead changes. Ubed even had to face great pressure in the second game when both players were neck-and-neck past the normal point limit.

After the match, Ubed admitted that the victory was not achieved easily.

"It was a very tight match and I am grateful to have been able to escape the pressure from Brian Yang."

Ubed also assessed that he still needs to improve his patience when building attacks. In the next round, he is scheduled to face Christo Popov from France.

The match has the potential to be a tough test because Ubed lost in their two previous meetings with Popov.

From the women's doubles category, the pair Febriana Dwipuji Kusuma/Meilysa Trias Puspitasari were the first to secure a spot in the round of 16.

The pair, familiarly known as Ana/Trias, defeated Chang Ching Hui/Yang Ching Tun from Chinese Taipei with scores of 21-17 and 21-15 on Tuesday (10/11/2026).

This victory is an important asset for Ana/Trias, who are trying to improve their consistency and maintain their chances of reaching the BWF World Tour Finals.

Trias admitted that there are still a number of things that need to be improved, especially when the match enters the final phase.

A positive result was also recorded by Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti.

The Tiwi/Fadia pair successfully eliminated Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara from Japan with scores of 21-14 and 21-13.

The victory boosted Tiwi/Fadia's confidence after previously winning the 2026 Hylo Open title in Germany.

Thus, Indonesia has secured two women's doubles pairs in the round of 16 of the 2026 Kumamoto Masters.

Different results were obtained by three Indonesian pairs in the mixed doubles sector.

Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah successfully advanced to the next round after defeating Ruben Garcia/Lucia Rodriguez from Spain with scores of 21-14 and 21-5.

The Indonesian pair was able to maintain pressure throughout the match and showed dominance in the second game.

However, the success of Amri/Nita was not followed by the other two pairs.

Dejan Ferdinansyah/Felisha Alberta Nathaniel Pasaribu had to acknowledge the superiority of the Chinese pair, Gao Jia Xuan/Wu Meng Ying, with scores of 20-22 and 14-21.

Meanwhile, Marwan Faza/Aisyah Salsabila Putri Pranata were eliminated after losing to host representatives Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi with scores of 16-21 and 10-21.

This result makes Amri/Nita the only Indonesian mixed doubles pair to continue their struggle into the round of 16.

One of the most surprising results came from the men's doubles sector.

Fajar Alfian/Muhammad Shohibul Fikri, who were the second seeds, failed to pass the first round after being defeated by Hiroki Okamura/Kyohei Yamashita from Japan.

Fajar/Fikri surrendered after a three-game battle with scores of 14-21, 21-11, and 27-29.

In the deciding game, the Indonesian pair actually led 19-13. However, that lead failed to be maintained after the Japanese pair fought back and forced a deuce.

Fajar admitted that the opponent's performance was very solid, especially in defending and handling critical points.

"This is a lesson for us going forward."

A similar fate was experienced by Sabar Karyaman Gutama/Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani who lost to the Chinese pair, Hu Ke Yuan/Liang Wei Keng, with scores of 21-23 and 16-21.

The two defeats ensured that Indonesia no longer has any men's doubles representatives in the round of 16.

In the women's singles sector, Putri Kusuma Wardani is scheduled to face Japanese player, Riko Gunji, on Wednesday (11/11/2026). The result of that match was not included in the recap confirmed at the time of writing this news.

Meanwhile, Muhamad Yusuf previously failed to pass the men's singles qualification round after being defeated by Yoo Tae Bin from South Korea with scores of 19-21 and 9-21.

The round of 16 of the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 is scheduled to take place on Thursday (12/11/2026), followed by the quarterfinals on Friday (13/11), semifinals on Saturday (14/11), and the final on Sunday (15/11).
